External links for this lesson, checked to load on 2026-11-13. Quoted regulatory and policy text in
the lesson comes from the local copies in `sources/`, not from these pages.

- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR Part 46, Protection of Human Subjects](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/part-46)**
  — the whole Common Rule. Use it for the parts our excerpt omits (exemptions, IRB review procedures,
  documentation of consent). Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 46.102, Definitions](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.102)** —
  research, human subject, private information, identifiable private information. Use it when
  someone asks "is this even human subjects research?" Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13
  (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 46.111, Criteria for IRB approval of research](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/46.111)**
  — what an IRB must determine, including the privacy and confidentiality criterion. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 164.512, Uses and disclosures not requiring authorization](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.512)**
  — paragraph (i) is the research pathway (waiver of authorization, preparatory reviews,
  decedents). Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 164.514, Other requirements relating to uses and disclosures of PHI](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.514)**
  — paragraph (e) is the limited data set and data use agreement. Paragraphs (a) and (b), which this
  lesson deliberately doesn't teach, cover de-identification. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 42 U.S.C. 241, Research and investigations generally](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/241)**
  — subsection (d) is the Certificate of Confidentiality statute. Read it with counsel when the
  question is how far a Certificate reaches. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIH Guide Notice NOT-OD-17-109, Changes to NIH Policy for Issuing Certificates of Confidentiality](https://grants.nih.gov/grants/guide/notice-files/NOT-OD-17-109.html)**
  — NIH's policy: automatic Certificates, the disclosure rules, and what recipients must do. Page
  title confirmed as "NOT-OD-17-109: Notice of Changes to NIH Policy for Issuing Certificates of
  Confidentiality." Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIH Grants & Funding: Certificates of Confidentiality (CoC)](https://grants.nih.gov/grants/policy/coc/welcome.htm)**
  — NIH's own overview page, the place to look for its current FAQs. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIH eRA: Certificates of Confidentiality Frequently Asked Questions](https://www.era.nih.gov/erahelp/Coc_Ext/Content/External/Introduction.htm)**
  — NIH's eRA help pages on its Certificate system, including who is covered automatically and who
  applies. Its system is for applications; the lesson's Lakeshore decision doesn't involve one.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **Back in the curriculum:** [Information governance in a covered entity](../../healthcare-security-and-privacy/information-governance-in-a-covered-entity/index.qmd),
  [The HIPAA Privacy Rule](../../healthcare-security-and-privacy/the-hipaa-privacy-rule/index.qmd),
  [Module 2, the vein-to-vein database and research extracts](../the-vein-to-vein-database-and-research-extracts/index.qmd).

- **[Certificates of Confidentiality Part 1: General Overview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wRgwdnHiuQE)**
  (U.S. Food and Drug Administration, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson:
  FDA's overview of Certificates of Confidentiality. FDA issues Certificates for research it
  regulates; NIH's policy governs NIH-funded research, so use it as background on the shared statute.
  Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200). The 2022 program-design
paper (Josephson et al., *Transfusion*) is the source for the single-IRB waiver statement; its
PubMed Central page returned a bot-check page to `curl` on the earlier modules, so it is not
re-listed here (module 1's resources page links it).

## Keep learning

Not official sources, and not authority for any regulatory claim.

- **[NIH "All About Grants" podcast: Certificates of Confidentiality (transcript)](https://grants.nih.gov/podcasts/All_About_Grants/episodes/Transcript-Certificates-of-Confidentiality.htm)**
  — an NIH human subjects officer explains what a Certificate is, when disclosure is and isn't
  allowed, and how to tell whether a study has one. It's NIH's own explainer but a podcast
  conversation, not policy text. The transcript page loaded with a generic page title and some
  garbled characters; the text mentions the speaker and topic. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

- **[UNC Privacy Office: HIPAA and Research (training slides, PDF)](https://research.unc.edu/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/HIPAA-Training_Research_6.16.2021.pdf)**
  — a university privacy office's training deck on how HIPAA applies to research. Useful for seeing
  how an institution explains the pathways to its researchers. A university's own practice, not a
  rule. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200; PDF).

- **[NIH eRA: About Certificates of Confidentiality](https://www.era.nih.gov/erahelp/CoC_Ext/Content/A-Introduction/Introduction.htm)**
  — NIH's short introduction to Certificates inside its Certificate-system help. Good as a one-page
  orientation before reading the statute. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).
